transcript: Then she went down the steps to the floor, because the board had asked every four that had stood the measure to stand on the floor of the graving while it was read. There were ninety-six of them, and the reserves behind, and they stood on the stone at the bottom of the dock in twenty-four rows of four, in the order of the standing after three boards, with Haldan license at the front and the twenty-fourth at the back by the floating gate. The tiers went up round them on three sides, full to the iron and glass roof, and the lamps had been lit along every tier, white and steady. At the seaward end, behind the twenty-fourth, the harbor breathed against the gate's black timber. Seven stood in the ninth row. Perrin had been let stand, by ask, on condition he did not stand long. He stood at the end of the row with his hand pressed to his side, and Anwen next to him, and Jude, and Kiva at the other end. Prue stood behind them with the reserves, with her capped hands folded in front of her, as Thrail folded hers.
